articles.title: Art Deco Classic
articles.summary: Rows of fan and sunburst motifs with radiating spokes, gilded symmetry on a soft base. A big high-contrast zigzag stripe that reads from far away like a racing chevron.
articles.what: 1920s Art Deco geometric fan and sunburst motif with radiating spokes and gilded symmetry — timeless Up close: The picture is identical to the lowercase art_deco render: thick silver-grey chevron zigzag bands about 45 px thick, repeating every 130 px, separated by black bands, with hard straight edges. Group: Abstract, Fractal & Paradigm. Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and open the PATTERN section.
Click Pattern 1 on this Layer to open the picker.
Open the group "Abstract, Fractal & Paradigm" or search for "Art Deco Classic", then click it.
Drag Scale below 1.00 until the repeats look fine on the car.
Switch Paint mode to Blend if you want to keep your paint colour.
tips: Sides and hood: chevrons point along the car and read as speed
Avoid small trim where the bands are too wide
High-contrast bands cut through numbers; use a number plate or keep numbers large and outlined.
Dark
Pairs well with: gloss black, deep navy, cream, dark green.
pitfalls: Not a fan or sunburst: the render shows only chevrons, though the description promises fans
Not fine linework: the bands are wide and flat
Avoid: too busy on small panels, muddy over mid-tone bases.
articles.intent_note: Pattern-design shelf: the structure of the pattern matters, not the colour it is printed in.
articles.paint_advice: Pattern contrast 58 out of 100: medium, pick a base colour that is clearly lighter or darker than the pattern. It covers about 32 percent of the tile, so a lot of base colour stays visible. Use Paint mode Blend to keep your colour; Overlay prints the pattern's own colours over it.
